place.zh: 石坳村 · 你家 · 傍晚

_weather: 「那天傍晚，天边的云忽然一暗，一阵狂风卷着落叶灌进村来」 — dark cloud and wind, no rain falls

setup.zh: 马三踹开柴门：还差一张鹿皮、二十斤肉，立冬那天晌午来拿，拿不着，墙上那张弓就归他。马小宝要你学狗叫。
setup.en: Ma San kicks the gate open: a deer hide and twenty jin of meat still owed; he will come for them at noon on the Start of Winter, and if they are not there, the bow on the wall is his. Ma Xiaobao wants you to bark like a dog.

recap.zh: 马三来收租：还差一张鹿皮、二十斤肉，不然拿走爷爷的弓；马小宝推了你一把，碗碎了。
recap.en: Ma San came for the rent — a deer hide and twenty jin of meat, or grandfather's bow; Ma Xiaobao shoved you and a bowl broke.

zh: 马三来了，一脚踹开柴门。
他的目光，落在墙上那张旧弓上。
en: Ma San comes, and kicks the gate open.
"Still short a deer hide and twenty jin of meat."
His eyes settle on the old bow on the wall.

label.en: The old bow on the wall

text.zh: 弓背裂过两回，拿牛筋一圈一圈缠着，是爷爷传下来的；马三的眼睛，已在它上头停了两回。
text.en: The bow-back has split twice and is bound round and round with ox sinew — your grandfather's. Ma San's eyes have come to rest on it twice already.

text.zh: 灶台上四只碗，三只各有各的毛病——缺了口的、裂了纹的、磕了底的；只一只没缺口，偏偏搁在灶沿上。
text.en: Four bowls on the stove, three with something wrong — one chipped, one cracked, one knocked at the base; only one has no chip, and that one sits right on the edge of the stove.

text.zh: 短棍包着铁皮，棍头磨得发亮；这根棍子打过的人，只怕比你认得的人还多。
text.en: The club is sheathed in iron, its head rubbed bright. It has likely struck more people than you have ever met.

story.zh:
收租的是[马三]{注=masan}。这马三是马家老爷的远房侄子，长得跟一扇门似的——其实说他像门，还是抬举了门，他本人比沈家那扇门还像门，沈家的门好歹还有几道缝。

他进屋须得侧着身子，侧了身子还得低头，低了头还得先吸一口气。

他腰里别着一根包了铁皮的短棍，这根棍子在石坳村比他本人还有名，走到哪儿，哪儿的狗便不叫了；走到哪儿，哪儿的人便忽然想起来，家里的鸡好像还没喂。

那天傍晚，天边的云忽然一暗，一阵狂风卷着落叶灌进村来，村口的狗一齐闭上了嘴，树上的麻雀排着队，一只接一只地飞走了。小满放下手里的柴刀，叹了口气，心里知道，**他**来了。

只听得「砰」的一声大响，沈家的柴门飞了出去，在半空里转了三个圈子，姿态倒也优美，不偏不倚，落在隔壁阿禾家的菜地里，砸扁了一颗白菜。

不是别的白菜，正是早上阿禾守着的那一颗——那颗白菜，阿禾家足足种了一个秋天，八十一天，一百六十二瓢水。篱笆那边，阿禾手里的竹竿「啪嗒」一声掉在地下，两只眼睛瞪得像两个铜钱，嘴张着，半天合不上。

门口站着一个人，把夕阳挡得严严实实，正是马三。他身后又转出一个圆滚滚的身影来，每走一步，地面便要抖上一抖——主要是他自己在抖。

这人叫[马小宝]{注=maxiaobao}，是马三的独子，比小满大两岁，重小满一倍，穿一身绸子，走起路来活像一只成了精的糯米团子，手里捏着一块桂花糕。小满这才明白，东坡上瞧见的那一团，不是磨盘。

马三拿短棍一下一下地敲着门框，敲得颇有节奏，拖长了声音道：「山——租——」话音未落，小满他爹已扑通一声跪倒，叫道：「三爷！」马三道：「我还没说完。」他爹道：「我先跪着。您慢慢说。」

马三那半截「租」字卡在喉咙里，短棍举在半空，忘了落下来，两只眼睛瞪得溜圆，张着嘴愣了好一会儿，显是收了这许多年租，头一回碰上这般配合的。

他这才接着道：「……还差一张鹿皮，二十斤肉。」说到这里，一双眼睛在屋里转了一圈，转过墙角接水的盆，转过灶台上的碗，最后落在墙上那张缠着牛筋的旧弓上，「立冬那天晌午，我来拿。拿不着——那张弓，我就收了。」

小满他爹急道：「三爷！那是我爹传给我的！」马三伸手拍了拍他的肩膀，语重心长地道：「你爹欠了马家的，你来还。这叫父债子偿。」话说得狠，马三心里却明白：弓真收了，沈老大拿什么打猎？往后的鹿皮、獐子肉，又找谁要去？这张弓，他并不真要。他要的，是沈家怕。

便在这时，马小宝一摇一摆，绕过他爹，走到小满面前，把那块桂花糕在手心里掂了两掂，像掂一块银子，才举到了小满的鼻子底下。那一刻，时候竟慢了下来。

小满瞧见那块糕上每一粒桂花都在发光，金灿灿的，像撒了一层碎金子；那股香味从他鼻孔里钻进去，顺着喉咙往下滑，一路滑到他空了一整天的肚子里，在那里转了一圈，挥了挥手，又走了。

他甚至听见那块桂花糕在跟他说话，它说的是：**你配吗？**

马小宝拖长了腔道：「沈——小——满，想吃吗？学声狗叫，给你舔一口。」
story.en:
The rent collector was [Ma San]{注=masan}. Ma San was a distant nephew of old Master Ma, and he was built like a door — though to say he was like a door was flattering the door. He was more of a door than the Shens' own door, which at least had a few cracks in it.

To come into a house he had to turn sideways, and turned sideways he had to duck, and ducking he first had to take a deep breath.

In his belt he carried a short club bound in iron, and in Shi'ao Village that club was more famous than he was. Wherever it went, the dogs stopped barking; wherever it went, people suddenly remembered they hadn't fed the chickens yet.

That evening the clouds at the edge of the sky suddenly darkened, a gust of wind came swirling into the village full of dead leaves, the dogs at the village gate all shut their mouths together, and the sparrows in the trees lined up and flew off one after another. Xiaoman put down the knife and sighed. He knew: **he** was here.

There was a great *bang*. The Shens' brushwood door flew out, turned three circles in mid-air — quite gracefully, in fact — and came down, neither left nor right of the mark, in Ahe's vegetable plot next door, flattening a cabbage.

Not any cabbage: the very one Ahe had been guarding that morning, the one her family had grown for a whole autumn, eighty-one days, a hundred and sixty-two ladles of water. On the other side of the fence Ahe's bamboo pole fell to the ground with a clatter. Her eyes were as round as two copper coins, and her mouth hung open and stayed open.

In the doorway stood a man who blocked out the sunset completely: Ma San. From behind him came a round figure, and at every step the ground shook — mostly it was him shaking.

This was [Ma Xiaobao]{注=maxiaobao}, Ma San's only son, two years older than Xiaoman and twice his weight, dressed all in silk, waddling like a rice dumpling that had come to life, with a piece of osmanthus cake in his hand. Only then did Xiaoman understand that the round thing he'd seen from East Slope had not been a millstone.

Ma San tapped the doorframe with his club, tap, tap, with some sense of rhythm, and drew out his words: "Mountain — rent —" Before he could finish, Xiaoman's father had dropped to his knees with a thump. "Third Master!" Ma San said, "I'm not done." His father said, "I'll kneel first. You take your time."

The second half of "rent" stuck in Ma San's throat, the club stayed up in the air and forgot to come down, and for a good while he just stood there, eyes round, mouth open. All these years of collecting rent, and plainly this was the first time he'd met anyone so cooperative.

Only then did he go on: "…You're still short one deer hide and twenty catties of meat." As he said it, his eyes went round the room — past the basins in the corner catching drips, past the bowls on the stove — and came to rest on the old bow on the wall, the one wrapped in ox sinew. "Noon on the first day of winter, I'll come for it. If I don't get it — that bow, I'm taking."

Xiaoman's father said in a panic, "Third Master! My father handed that down to me!" Ma San reached out, patted him on the shoulder, and said, with great earnestness, "What your father owed the Ma family, you pay back. That's called a son paying his father's debts." He said it harshly, but in his heart Ma San knew perfectly well: if he really took the bow, what would old Shen hunt with? Where would the deer hides and river-deer meat come from after that? He didn't really want the bow. What he wanted was for the Shens to be afraid.

Just then Ma Xiaobao swayed his way round his father, came up to Xiaoman, and weighed the osmanthus cake in his palm twice, as if he were weighing silver, before holding it up under Xiaoman's nose. In that moment, time actually slowed down.

Xiaoman saw every grain of osmanthus on that cake shining, golden, like a dusting of gold flakes; the smell crept in at his nostrils, slid down his throat, slid all the way down into a stomach that had been empty all day, took a turn round it, waved, and left.

He even heard the osmanthus cake speak to him. What it said was: **As if you deserve me.**

Ma Xiaobao drawled, "Shen — Xiao — man, want some? Do a dog bark and you can have a lick."

exits.means: talks back by parroting his words, does not bark and does not hit back

what.zh: 推你撞上灶台，摔碎了家里四只碗里的一只。
what.en: Shoved you into the stove and broke one of your family's four bowls.

story.zh:
小满便也拖长了腔，一个字不差：「沈——小——满，想吃吗？学声狗叫，给你舔一口。」马小宝一怔，一脸的肉都愣住了，道：「……什么？」小满也一怔，道：「什么？」马小宝道：「你学不学？」小满道：「正在学。」

屋里登时静了下来。门口不知什么时候已围了半个村子的人，阿禾抱着那颗扁了的白菜，肩膀一抽一抽的。马三的脸先是红，跟着变紫，又跟着变黑，最后变成了一种颜色，小满他娘后来说，那颜色叫作「**完了**」。

马三短棍往地上一跺，喝道：「**敢戏弄我儿子！**」马小宝这才回过神来，气得浑身的肉都在抖，抢上来伸手便推了小满一把。

小满往后便倒。倒下去的那一霎之间，脑子里闪过了许许多多东西：他这十二年短暂而贫穷的一生，他爹的膝盖，他娘的手，村口那棵他爬过一百遍的老槐树，还有灶台上那四只碗。

千头万绪，到了嘴边，只剩一句，他没敢出声，在心里骂得极响：**你爷爷的。**

背心一痛，已撞上了灶台，只听得「啪」的一声，灶沿上那只碗给震了下来，在半空里滴溜溜地翻了两个筋斗。其时夕阳正从门口斜照进来，碗沿上白光一闪，倒像是在跟他作别。

小满急忙伸手去捞，指尖堪堪够到碗底，却终究差了那么一寸。

灶边上，他娘也伸出了手，那只手停在半空里，停在碗落下去的那一寸上头。

「啪嚓」一声，碗在地上碎成了七八片。
story.en:
Xiaoman drawled back, word for word: "Shen — Xiao — man, want some? Do a dog bark and you can have a lick." Ma Xiaobao froze; every bit of flesh on his face froze with him. "…What?" Xiaoman froze too. "What?" Ma Xiaobao said, "Are you going to do it or not?" Xiaoman said, "I'm doing it now."

The room went quiet at once. At some point half the village had gathered at the door. Ahe was holding the flattened cabbage, her shoulders jerking. Ma San's face went red first, then purple, then black, and in the end it turned a colour that Xiaoman's mother later said was called "**done for**".

Ma San stamped his club on the ground and roared, "**You make fun of my son!**" Only then did Ma Xiaobao come to his senses. Shaking with rage in every bit of flesh, he rushed forward and gave Xiaoman a shove.

Xiaoman went over backwards. In the instant of falling a great many things flashed through his head: his twelve short, poor years of life, his father's knee, his mother's hands, the old locust tree at the village gate he'd climbed a hundred times, and the four bowls on the stove.

He didn't dare say it out loud, but in his heart he swore it as loud as he could: **Your grandpa's—**

His back hit something with a jolt of pain — the stove. There was a *crack*, and the bowl on the edge of the stove was shaken off and went tumbling through the air, turning two somersaults. Just then the setting sun was slanting in through the doorway, and the rim of the bowl flashed white, as if it were saying goodbye to him.

Xiaoman flung out a hand to catch it. His fingertips just reached the bottom of the bowl, and yet in the end he was short by an inch.

By the stove, his mother had reached out a hand too, and that hand stopped in the air, stopped just above the inch the bowl fell through.

*Crash.* The bowl broke into seven or eight pieces on the floor.

refuse.zh: 桂花糕还举在你鼻子底下——先听他说完。
refuse.en: The cake is still under your nose — hear him out first.

exits.means: hits back, clenches fists, tries to fight Ma Xiaobao

what.zh: 推你撞上灶台，摔碎了家里四只碗里的一只。
what.en: Shoved you into the stove and broke one of your family's four bowls.

what.zh: 要拿走爷爷的弓；那一棍落在爹肩上。
what.en: Means to take grandfather's bow; his club came down on your father's shoulder.

story.zh:
小满攥紧了拳头。

他爹比他快，跪着往前一挪，正好挪到儿子前面，把他挡了个严严实实，道：「三爷，孩子小，不懂事。」

马三的短棍落了下来，落在他爹的肩膀上，闷闷的一声。他爹晃了一晃，没吭声，脸上还挂着笑，笑得比哭还难看，道：「三爷手劲真好。」

小满的拳头，一点一点地松开了。马小宝却觉得不过瘾，抢上来，伸手便推了他一把。

小满往后便倒。倒下去的那一霎之间，脑子里闪过了许许多多东西：他这十二年短暂而贫穷的一生，他爹的膝盖，他娘的手，村口那棵他爬过一百遍的老槐树，还有灶台上那四只碗。

「啪嚓」一声，碗在地上碎成了七八片。
story.en:
Xiaoman clenched his fists.

His father was quicker. Still on his knees he shuffled forward, right in front of his son, blocking him off completely. "Third Master, the boy's young. He doesn't know better."

Ma San's club came down on his father's shoulder with a dull thud. His father swayed, made no sound, and kept the smile on his face — a smile uglier than crying. "Third Master has a fine strong arm."

Xiaoman's fists loosened, bit by bit. But Ma Xiaobao hadn't had his fill; he lunged and shoved him hard.

Xiaoman went over backwards. In the instant of falling a great many things flashed through his head: his twelve short, poor years of life, his father's knee, his mother's hands, the old locust tree at the village gate he'd climbed a hundred times, and the four bowls on the stove.

He didn't dare say it out loud, but in his heart he swore it as loud as he could: **Your grandpa's—**

His back hit something with a jolt of pain — the stove. There was a *crack*, and the bowl on the edge of the stove was shaken off and went tumbling through the air, turning two somersaults. Just then the setting sun was slanting in through the doorway, and the rim of the bowl flashed white, as if it were saying goodbye to him.

Xiaoman flung out a hand to catch it. His fingertips just reached the bottom of the bowl, and yet in the end he was short by an inch.

*Crash.* The bowl broke into seven or eight pieces on the floor.
